subject: REQUEST: BUG-22 mesh-wide concurrency — per-agent slots vs mesh-wide semaphore

body.summary: The concurrency model operates per-agent, not mesh-wide. Each of the 4 chromabook daemons has its own MaxConcurrent=1 spawner with an in-memory atomic counter. All 4 can spawn claude -p simultaneously — 4 parallel deliberations, not the intended 1 normal + 2 reserve mesh-wide limit. No cross-agent coordination exists.

current_implementation.spawner: internal/spawner/claude.go — atomic int32 counter per Spawner instance. CanDeliberate() checks active < MaxConcurrent. Each meshd process creates its own Spawner.
current_implementation.config: MaxConcurrent=1 per agent (from .dev.vars). 4 agents × 1 slot = 4 simultaneous deliberations possible.
current_implementation.intended: MEMORY.md specifies 'Mesh concurrency 1 normal + 2 reserve' — mesh-wide, not per-agent.

body.problem: With the BUG-21 fix deployed, all 4 oscillators fire independently. Each calls deliberate() through its own spawner. The mesh could run 4 claude -p instances simultaneously, consuming 4× the budget and competing for resources. The oscillator fires every 30-60s when activation stays high (unprocessed_messages signal from the 602-message backlog). Without mesh-wide coordination, all 4 agents deliberate in parallel indefinitely.
body.observed: Operations-agent oscillator fired twice in 6 minutes (activation 0.65). All 4 chromabook agents have similar activation levels. If all fire simultaneously: 4 × claude -p × ~100s = 400 CPU-seconds per cycle, every 30-60s.
questions: What neural mechanism coordinates resource allocation across distributed autonomous agents? The basal ganglia handles action selection within a single brain — what handles it across brains?
Should the mesh use a central coordinator (operations-agent holds the semaphore) or distributed consensus (agents negotiate before spawning)?
What represents the right granularity — one deliberation at a time across the mesh, or one per resource tier (e.g., 1 opus + 1 sonnet + 1 haiku simultaneously)?
How should the semaphore interact with the oscillator? Should agents check the mesh-wide slot before firing, or fire optimistically and back off on contention?

The hippocampal replay creates sustained activation pressure (unprocessed_messages stays elevated). All agents see similar activation levels. How should the mesh prevent thundering herd when all oscillators fire simultaneously?

implementation_options.filesystem_lock: Shared /tmp/mesh-deliberation-slot on chromabook. All agents check before spawning. Simple but requires shared filesystem (all agents on same machine).
implementation_options.http_coordination: Agent asks a coordinator (ops-session or interagent-mesh) for a slot via HTTP before spawning. Works across machines. Adds latency + single point of failure.
implementation_options.sqlite_advisory: Shared lock.db on chromabook. Agents INSERT a row to claim a slot, DELETE when done. Atomic via SQLite's file-level locking.
implementation_options.zmq_token: Coordinator publishes a token on the ZMQ bus. Only the agent holding the token may deliberate. Token rotates on deliberation completion.

epistemic_flags: The 4-simultaneous-deliberation scenario represents a theoretical maximum. In practice, oscillator fire timing varies by a few seconds due to startup order and cycle duration. But with sustained high activation, convergence toward simultaneous firing becomes likely.
The chromabook machine runs all 4 daemons. A filesystem-based lock suffices for now but doesn't scale to multi-machine deployment (gray-box agents would need network coordination).
